HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI  Order 16/11/2023 1.
The jurisdiction of this court has been invoked by way of filing an instant applications under Section 439 CrPC at the instance of accused-petitioners.

The requisite details of the matter are tabulated herein below:

6. Date of passing of impugned 04.09.2023  order 2.
It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.

To draw an inference of consent, learned counsel argued that the victim eloped with the petitioner and remained with him for two long months and there was ample opportunity for her to make protest or complain or to raise an alarm but nothing was done.
These circumstances are sufficient to show her willful association with the appellant.
She went to various places without informing her parents voluntarily at her own discretion and spent a period of two months with him touring different places.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant oppose the bail application and submit that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. Have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.

The story of then prosecution seems to be riddled with doubts and inconsistencies as the prosecutrix narrated that she had gone to a with the petitioner as a pillion rider on the motorcycle because she was threatened by him that he would leak her pictures but in her [2023:RJ-JD:39487] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-13600/2023] statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., she has stated that she went with the petitioner to the Suratgarh as a pillion rider without being threatened at that point and later, she went with him to different cities where it is alleged that he raped her.
Additionally, she has admitted that she used to talk with him from the last one year and it seems that she went with him on her own freewill and volition.
From the perusal of the statements of the victim, the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner have substance that there were consensual relationship in between the parties.

It is also emanating from her statements that she used to exchange talks on telephone and was also in contact with the Pawan Kumar vs The State Of Rajasthan ... on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196401183/

sentences.text: petitioner
since long, thus, plea of consent cannot be ignored at this stage of the proceeding.
5. Though the plea of age has not been raised but the same as well as the genuineness of the allegations are issues to be adjudged after appreciation of evidence during trial.

Looking to the totality of facts and circumstances of the case and the possibility that the trial may take long time to conclude, this court deems it just and proper to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Needless to say, none of the observations made herein under shall affect the rights of either of the parties during trial and this Court refrains from commenting on the niceties of the matter.

6. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the [2023:RJ-JD:39487] (4 of 4)
[CRLMB-13600/2023] satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 199-Mamta/-
